Palworld is one of those games that will suck you in and have you wondering 'when did the sun set?'. Bordom is hard to find due to the many ways you can enjoy the content. Board of working on your pals? Go explore and see the awesome cratures thruout the world. Want some action? Head to a tower and take on a boss or maybe find a portal to a boss Pal lair. Farm for food and build facilities to give you pals something to do. The graphics bring a nice fantasy feel to the world. 

 Not everything is perfect. The terrain has a lot of obvious copy paste going on. Pals getting stuck on roofs or not being able to path to something cus it on the other side of the wall. Settings not being describe plainly enough leading to bad combat experiences or slow leveling issues. Mounts feeling slow or clunky.

This game is obviously still being developed, but you can tell it has a strong foundation. There are ideas in the works and it can be seen in game with every patch. The devs are doing well to show where they are taking the game.

Well Time for my 100+ hr review it's essentially Pokemon and Ark had a baby you base build, craft, and catch and battle with these creatures called Pals the game is a little buggy but the developers are slowly fixing them piece by piece like I had Pal spheres (basically Pokeballs) in my inventory and I would go too throw 1 but nothing would happen I had to restart to fix  the game is progressive and slowly gets harder as you go along they have these Boss Towers for me the first one was easy but I struggled a little at the 2nd anyways graphics are good the multiplayer aspect is fun and the grind can be real especially in mid-endgame I did receive this as a gift but I would 100% recommend buying especially if your like me and been waiting years for a Pokemon Like multiplayer game

I don't know, I don't have a lot of clever words to say about this. The world just felt empty and dull from the moment I booted up the game, the pals also kind of clashing in design choice to the world itself making everything feel plastic and off-putting, the world itself seeming like it was pasted from recycled assets and the environment design being random and haphazard. There's no real goal or anything either, you're just kind of set upon the world and that's it. The progression system felt a bit linear, and rather than having to like 'puzzle my way through it', it just felt like "if I input x amount of time, I'll inevitably get to y level", which is dull. I don't know, I don't get the hype, but I don't have to I suppose.
